To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the force needed to deform nanometer-scale Au connective necks is 10 to 100 times higher than the theoretical value calculated by the JKR theory, and that this force is constant during the plastic deformation of the neck.
the conductance of Au connective necks increases in steps as the tip is retracted from the substrate, each step corresponding to the plastic deformation of the neck.
the conductance of the neck decreases by a factor of 2.5 when the neck is compressed from 1 to about 1/4 of its initial length.
